title: C1153 — Left-front height sensor connector
introduction:
For the left-front height sensor, I start with the identity table before following any wire: CNumber and Description establish which reference is open. The connector drawing then supplies cavity labels, and the pin table gives each label its circuit identity. Think of the circuit number as the wire's name tag; its color is another identifying detail, not the whole introduction.

Read this page as a guide to the drawing, its unchanged circuit labels and the pigtail catalog. Physical access, connector release, electrical testing and replacement require their own instructions. The drawing does not specify a terminal-side or wire-side view. Box, Cols, Size and Used have no supplied decoding key, and Gauge has no stated convention; retain those entries without treating them as dimensions or wire-selection rules.

edits.why: The housing feature sits above the row of circular cavities in the drawing, with projecting features at either side. I use those shapes to recognize the illustration's page orientation and its printed cavity labels to find the table rows. This does not establish which side of a physical connector faces the viewer. Fpn and Harness Id associate the drawing with its listed shell and harness.

edits.text: Trace each cavity through the pin table
edits.why: Read across the row whose Cavity label matches the drawing. Circuit Number identifies the circuit, Color and Gauge record wire information, Function gives the listed role, and Terminal Part Number identifies the terminal entry. The height-position function identifies the sensor-related connection. Retain the controller and USB diagnostic wording literally; those labels and their plus/minus marks do not establish a supply voltage, test method or USB connection instruction. A blank Qualifier adds no further condition.

A pigtail combines a connector and attached wire leads for harness repair. Keep each row's Number, Service Part and Engineering Shell associated with that row. Gauge, Material and Cavities describe the entry, while Image names its associated file. Matching shell information helps relate the catalog entries to the connector, but it does not settle kit selection, wire substitution or how a repair is performed.
